episodic.text: hoi, just set up my Lumio hub on the barge last week. took me a while to find where to plug it in but its working now i think
Welcome James! Great to hear you got it up and running. Barges can be a bit tricky for placement — how are the signal levels looking in the app?
the app says 2 bars on the bedroom strip light. is that enough? the hull is steel so maybe thats the problem
Hub v1 signal detected at moderate strength on node LX-04 (bedroom strip). Steel hull interference noted in environment profile.
2 bars should be fine for basic on/off and dimming. Steel hulls do eat signal a bit. If you start getting dropouts try moving the hub a little closer to the centre of the barge
ok thanks. also the app is in english but id prefer dutch, how do i change that
Go to Settings > App Preferences > Language and pick Nederlands. Should take effect straight away without needing to restart.
ah found it, thanks. one more thing — i connected 3 bulbs in the woonkamer but only 2 show up
Can you try a manual rescan? Pull down on the Devices screen. Sometimes the third bulb just needs a moment, especially if you added them quickly one after another.
ja that worked, all 3 there now. gezellig
its getting cold already, typical dutch autumn. set the living room lights to warm white in the evening and its actually really nice on the water
That warm white setting at 2700K is perfect for those dark canal evenings. Glad it is working well for you!
had a shore power cut last night around midnight, maybe 20 minutes. when power came back the hub was blinking orange and two bulbs didnt respond
Hub power cycle detected. Nodes LX-01 and LX-02 failed to re-register after restoration. Automatic re-sync attempted, partial success.
Sorry about that, brownouts and sudden cuts can confuse the hub a bit. Try holding the reset button on each bulb for 5 seconds to re-pair them. Shouldnt lose your settings.
reset worked. is this going to happen every time the power goes out? we get cuts here maybe once a month at the marina
Hub v1 doesnt have a battery backup unfortunately. Most of the time it recovers cleanly but occasionally a bulb or two needs a nudge. Its a known limitation — something Hub v2 handles better actually
hmm interesting. how much is the v2
The Hub v2 is €89 for existing customers. It has better brownout recovery, wider Zigbee range and a few other extras. No pressure though, v1 handles most things just fine.
ill think about it. not in a hurry
my daughter Anouk is visiting this weekend. she wants to set the lights to some kind of disco mode for saturday night lol. is there a party scene or something
Ha! Yes, there is a Dynamic Color scene under Scenes > Entertainment. You can set the speed and intensity. Fair warning, on a barge the neighbors might also enjoy the light show through the portholes
haha ja probably. Anouk loved it by the way. she wants her own Lumio now
the app crashed twice this weekend when switching scenes quickly. android phone, fairly new. just freezes and i have to restart it
App crash events logged on account — two rapid scene-switch crashes on Android client version noted. Flagged for mobile team.
Thanks for flagging that, its a known issue when flipping scenes too fast on Android. A fix is in the pipeline. For now just give it a second between scene changes and it should be stable.
december now, its really dark by 4pm. i made a schedule — lights come on at 15:45 every day which is great. feels less depressing coming home to a lit barge
That is a great use of schedules. You can also link it to local sunset time in the schedule settings so it adjusts automatically through the season without you changing it.
oh i didnt know that. let me try it
ja works perfectly! it shifted the time already today. nice feature
got a bill notification — it says my subscription renews next month. I thought the hub v1 was a one-time purchase, why is there a subscription

Good question. The hub hardware is a one-time purchase, yes. The subscription covers cloud scheduling, remote access and the scene library. The basic plan is what you are on — €2.99 a month. You would have seen it at signup but easy to miss.
ah okay, i probably clicked past it. not a big deal i suppose. is there a free tier
There is a free tier yes, but it loses remote access and limits you to 3 schedules. Given how you use it I think the basic plan is worth keeping, but your call entirely.
okay ill keep it. merry christmas by the way, the barge looks really festive with the warm lights and some candles. very cosy
That sounds wonderful, James. Fijne feestdagen! Enjoy the season on the water.
new year, another shore power cut. this one was longer, maybe an hour. hub recovered fine this time actually, all lights came back on their own
Good news — looks like the hub found the bulbs cleanly after this one. Maybe the longer gap gave everything time to fully reset before reconnecting.
ja maybe. still a bit annoying that its always a lottery. the marina really needs to sort their electrics but getting an electrician to come to floating moorings is a nightmare here
january is freezing, the canal almost iced over near the bow this morning. got the lights on a really dim warm scene all day, kind of like permanent candlelight mode. working nicely
That sounds really atmospheric. You could save that as a custom scene so you can trigger it in one tap when the cold sets in each year.
good idea, done. called it Ijsdag haha
Anouk came by and noticed the bedroom bulb is flickering a little. not sure if its the bulb or the dimmer setting
Flickering at low dim levels is usually the bulb hitting the lower end of its range. Try setting the minimum brightness floor to about 15% in the bulb settings — that usually clears it up.
that fixed it, thanks. Anouk says hi by the way and wants to know if Lumio does outdoor lights because she wants them for her student apartment balcony
Tell Anouk we have an outdoor strip and a couple of weatherproof bulb options in the shop. They pair to any existing hub.
tried to access the app remotely from my phone when i was in Rotterdam for work. it just said hub offline. but when i got home the hub was clearly on and working fine
Remote connectivity check on account: hub showed intermittent cloud heartbeat loss during the 14:00-15:30 window noted. Likely marina router hiccup.

Looks like your marina router had a brief cloud disconnect that afternoon — the hub itself was fine locally. These are usually short-lived. If it keeps happening it might be worth checking whether the marina wifi is stable or if you need a separate connection for the hub.
the marina wifi is terrible honestly. i use a 4G router of my own for the barge internet. maybe i should just make sure the hub is on that one and not the marina network
Yes, that is a much better setup. Move the hub to your 4G router network and you should get much more reliable remote access. Just re-enter the wifi credentials in Settings > Hub > Network.
switched it over, works well now. should have done that from the start
good morning, hub rebooted itself again overnight. third time this month i think

Morning James. That pattern of overnight reboots usually points to a power interruption — likely a brief shore-supply dip. The hub is recovering fine each time, but I can log these so we have a record if you want to escalate with the marina.
yes please do that. the marina manager keeps saying the supply is stable but it clearly isnt
Hub v1 connectivity dropped for 14 minutes at approximately 02:40 local time. Device self-recovered. Shore-power fluctuation suspected.
anouk is coming this weekend, can i make a scene that turns on the fairy lights in her cabin and sets heating to 20 degrees? she always complains its cold down there

Absolutely. You can build that as a Scene in the app — name it something like 'Anouk arrives', set the cabin bulbs and the thermostat together, then either trigger it manually or tie it to a time on Friday evening. Want me to walk you through it?
yeah walk me through it, i always forget which menu it is
ok got it working i think. tested it and the lights came on. heating i am not 100% sure, the thermostat icon just spins

The spinning icon usually means the hub is waiting for a response from the thermostat. Can you check if the thermostat shows as 'online' in Devices? Sometimes after a reboot it needs a minute to re-pair.
it says online now and the scene ran properly. must have just been slow. all good
anouk loved the lights by the way. she said the barge finally feels like a proper home haha
That's great to hear! Fairy lights on a barge does sound pretty perfect honestly.
quick question — my lumio app keeps switching the interface to english even though i have my phone set to dutch. is there a setting somewhere

There is a language setting inside the app itself under Profile > Preferences — it doesn't always inherit from the phone OS. Set it to Nederlands there and it should stick. Let me know if it keeps reverting.
found it, changed it. though honestly some of the dutch translations are a bit weird. 'slimme scène' sounds strange to me. minor thing
User flagged Dutch translation feedback — 'slimme scène' label noted as feeling unnatural. Passed to localisation team.
its getting properly warm now, canal is lovely in the evenings. started leaving the deck hatch open at night which means my motion sensor keeps triggering the hallway light. bit annoying
You can narrow the sensitivity or set an active schedule on that sensor — so it only triggers between say sunset and midnight and ignores movement after that. Would that work for you?
yes that sounds good. midnight to 07:00 off would be ideal
Done, or rather — you can set that in the sensor settings under 'Active hours'. Let me know if the path is unclear and I can guide you step by step.
managed it myself actually, quite proud. no more random hallway light at 2am
a boat from the sailing club was playing very loud music last night and i jokingly told my hub to turn off their lights. obviously didnt work haha. would be a feature though
Ha — neighbourhood control is unfortunately not in the roadmap. Glad the hub at least behaved itself.
billing question — i was charged twice in april i think. or maybe march. the amounts look the same on my bank statement
I can look into that for you. Can you confirm the email address on your Lumio account and roughly which months you're seeing duplicates for? I'll flag it for billing review.
its james.vandermeer at the gmail one. i think it was two charges around the same week, maybe subscription renewal hit twice
Billing review initiated for account james.vandermeer@gmail.com. Possible duplicate subscription charge identified — credit note process started.
billing team sorted it, got a credit. thanks for pushing that through
the tulips along the canal bank are completely gone now, summer happened fast. the blinds routine i set in spring still runs every morning — does it make sense to keep it or should i adjust

Worth reviewing — summer sunrise is earlier and the angle changes, so the schedule that worked in April might be opening blinds when you still want privacy. What time does your current routine trigger?
06:15. yeah thats too early now that i think about it. i will push it to 07:30
hub went offline for about 40 minutes this afternoon. shore power again i assume. everything came back fine but the smart plugs in the galley lost their schedules

Shore-power interruption confirmed at 14:12 local, duration approximately 38 minutes. Hub recovery normal. Three smart plug schedules cleared from memory — known issue with extended outages on Hub v1.

This is a known Hub v1 limitation — longer outages can wipe plug schedules from local memory. Hub v2 holds schedules in persistent storage so this wouldn't happen. Might be worth factoring that in if you're still thinking about upgrading.
yeah i keep going back and forth on the v2. the price is the thing. and finding an electrician who will come to a moored barge is a whole project on its own. last time i waited six weeks
The v2 hub swap itself doesn't require an electrician — it just replaces the hub unit and you re-pair your devices. No wiring involved unless you're adding new hardwired kit.
oh really? i assumed it needed to be wired in. that changes things a bit. so i could basically just do it myself on a sunday afternoon?
Exactly — it's plug and play for the hub itself. The migration tool in the app should carry over most of your scenes and device settings too. Takes most people under an hour.
anouk is staying for a whole week this time, she is between jobs. she keeps changing all my lighting scenes and i dont know how to lock them or at least get notified when something changes
You can set Anouk's account to 'Member' rather than 'Admin' access — Members can trigger scenes but can't edit or delete them. Would that work without causing a family argument?
haha probably best not to mention it to her. ill just quietly change it. she means well
had a nice week with anouk. she actually got quite into the lumio app, was asking about the hub v2 herself and whether it supports better colour bulbs. she has opinions
Hub v2 does support the full extended colour range bulbs, yes — and the response time is noticeably faster. Sounds like Anouk might be your best argument for upgrading.
she literally said 'papa just buy the v2 already' so maybe she is right. i will think about it more seriously
app crashed three times today while i was trying to edit a scene. just closes itself. iphone, latest ios
App crash reported by user on iOS, scene editing flow. Crash logs requested.
Sorry about that James. A fix for that crash in the scene editor went out recently — can you check you're on the latest app version in the App Store? Should be resolved after updating.
updated it and its fine now. should have tried that first i suppose
its getting darker earlier already, autumn coming. put the 'evening canal' scene back on — warm lights at 18:30, dims at 22:00. feels good to have that back
That sounds really cosy. Barge life in early autumn with the right lighting must be something.
ok i think i am finally going to order the hub v2. anouk convinced me and honestly the schedule-loss thing after the power cuts has happened twice more. ready to just do it

Great decision James — especially given your shore-power situation. I can help you through the migration whenever it arrives. The process is straightforward and your existing scenes should transfer cleanly. Let me know when you're ready.

procedural.name: hub_v1_brownout_recovery
procedural.trigger_text: my lights stopped responding after a power dip or brownout on the barge
procedural.description: Step-by-step recovery procedure for Hub v1 losing connectivity or becoming unresponsive after a shore-supply brownout at Sixhaven.

steps.instruction: Ask James whether the Hub v1 LED is off, solid, or flashing, and whether any other 12V or 230V devices on the barge also lost power briefly.
Recall known Hub v1 behaviour on under-voltage events: the hub may lock up and require a full power cycle rather than a soft reboot.
Instruct James to unplug the Hub v1 power adapter from the shore-supply socket, wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in and wait 2 minutes for full boot.
Ask James to open the Lumio app and confirm whether the hub is back online and lights are responding.
If the hub is still offline after the power cycle, escalate to Tier 2 with notes: Hub v1, shore-supply brownout, Amsterdam-Noord barge, LED state, and steps already taken.

procedural.name: hub_v1_to_v2_upgrade_assessment
procedural.trigger_text: should I upgrade my hub or is my old hub good enough
procedural.description: Consultative playbook to help James assess whether upgrading from Hub v1 to Hub v2 is worthwhile given his casual usage, brownout environment, and occasional weekend use with daughter Anouk.

steps.instruction: Recall Hub v1 vs Hub v2 feature differences, particularly improved power-resilience circuitry, faster reconnect after outages, and any v1 end-of-support timeline.
Ask James how often he experiences brownouts and whether missed automations or slow app response are causing him frustration.
Ask whether Anouk controls lights independently via her own app profile on weekends, since Hub v2 supports more concurrent app sessions.

Summarise upgrade benefits relevant to James: better brownout recovery, longer software support, and smoother multi-user weekends with Anouk. Confirm whether he wants a quote or a trial period option.
If James wants to proceed, escalate to sales team with context: Hub v1 owner, barge shore-supply environment, casual user, daughter co-user on weekends.

procedural.name: weekend_guest_app_access_setup
procedural.trigger_text: my daughter wants to control the lights from her phone when she visits
procedural.description: Playbook for setting up Anouk as a secondary app user on James's Lumio account so she can control lights on the barge during weekend visits.

steps.instruction: Recall the Lumio guest or secondary-user invitation flow for Hub v1, including any limitations on the number of secondary users.
Ask James whether Anouk already has the Lumio app installed and a Lumio account, or whether she needs to create one first.
Guide James to open the Lumio app, go to Settings, select Home Members or Share Access, and enter Anouk's email address to send her an invitation.
Ask James to confirm Anouk received the invitation email and accepted it, then have her open the app to verify the barge home appears in her account.
If the invitation does not arrive or the home does not appear for Anouk, escalate to Tier 2 with account details and note the Hub v1 secondary-user limitation as a possible cause.

procedural.name: hub_v1_offline_moored_environment_check
procedural.trigger_text: my hub keeps going offline even when the power seems fine
procedural.description: Diagnostic playbook for intermittent Hub v1 offline events specific to a barge mooring context, covering Wi-Fi signal, power quality, and physical environment factors at Sixhaven.

steps.instruction: Ask James how far the Wi-Fi router is from the Hub v1 on the barge, whether the router is also on shore power, and whether the hub is near any metal bulkheads or engine compartments.
Recall known Hub v1 sensitivities: marginal Wi-Fi signal causes frequent drops, and metal hulls on barges are a documented signal-attenuation factor.
Ask James to check the Lumio app event log or hub LED behaviour to determine whether the dropouts happen at specific times such as evenings when shore-supply load is highest.
Recommend James move the router closer to the hub or add a Wi-Fi extender, and suggest a UPS or line conditioner on the shore-supply feed to smooth brownouts before they reach the hub.
Ask James to monitor for 48 hours after any changes and report whether offline events have reduced in frequency.
If dropouts persist after environmental improvements, escalate to Tier 2 with full diagnostic notes: barge metal hull, shore-supply brownouts, Wi-Fi distance, Hub v1 firmware version.
